text: You want to refute the universally quantified claim 'for all n, P(n).' What suffices?
choices: Proving that P(n) fails for infinitely many n
Proving ¬P(n) for a single arbitrary (variable) n
Exhibiting one specific n for which P(n) is false — a counterexample
Showing that P(n) holds for some n
explanation: A universal ∀n P(n) is refuted by a single explicit counterexample — one concrete n with ¬P(n) — because its negation is ∃n ¬P(n). You need not find infinitely many. Proving ¬P(n) for an arbitrary n would establish ∀n ¬P(n), which is stronger than required; and showing P holds for some n confuses refuting the claim with confirming an instance.
